chunks: And in the narration of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, with his chain of transmission, he said:

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام said: “A man may alter his bequest: he may free the one whom he had ordered to be given ownership, and give ownership to the one whom he had ordered to be freed; and he may give to the one whom he had deprived, and deprive the one whom he had given to, so long as he has not retracted from it.”

key_terms.حَرَمَهُ: deprived him or withheld from him

ai.seo_question: Can a person change the terms of his will in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the testator’s authority to alter the terms of his bequest. It indicates that changes in matters such as manumission, transfer of ownership, giving, and withholding are valid within the scope of his will so long as he has not revoked that act.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5460 - In the narration of Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman with his chain of transmission,

Imam Ali ibn Al-Hussain (as) said:
"A man has the right to alter his will. He may free the one he had initially ordered to be owned, and he may grant ownership to the one he had initially ordered to be freed. He may give to the one he had previously deprived and deprive the one he had previously granted, as long as he has not retracted from his decision."
